prob.title: Why most HYROX plans fail
p1.d: A fast 10 km says little. After burpees and sleds your legs are compromised — without specific work you lose 20–60 s per km in the second half.
p2.d: Most calculators only look at your running. Sleds, lunges and wall balls decide 35–45 % of your time — and that is exactly where most athletes have the biggest gains.
p3.d: Generic plans stack volume and impact without looking at how you recover. Achilles and calves pay the price in week 6.
sol.title: Six things Benchmrk does differently
s1.d: Your finish time = 8 runs + 8 stations + Roxzone, from your ratings, PRs and benchmark splits. You see where the minutes are.
s2.d: Heart-rate zones on your own threshold HR (Friel %LTHR), capped at your max HR. No fixed numbers from someone else.
s3.d: Threshold test, threshold endurance, compromised pacing, pace-decay test and a full dress rehearsal recalibrate your paces — corrected for heart rate.
s4.d: Log pace, HR and RPE. Twice too slow at high HR? Targets ease off. Stiff tendons in the morning? Impact days switch to low-impact.
s5.d: Team code, one shared prediction, a split per station from both partners' times and a shared sim day.
s6.d: Weekly station strength aimed at your two weakest stations, progressing towards your division's race weights.

sci.title: What the plan is built on
sci1: VO₂max, aerobic training volume and body-fat % correlate most with HYROX finish time; runs are roughly 60 % of the race for recreational athletes.
sci2: HYROX is mostly horizontal work — running, sleds and carries — and needs specific training rather than generic CrossFit-style sessions.
sci3: Heart-rate zones as a percentage of your own lactate-threshold heart rate.
sci4: Official station weights per division, from Open women to Pro men.

faq.title: Questions
q1: I don't know my threshold heart rate.
a1: Use your Garmin estimate, or run 30 minutes as hard as you can sustain alone: your average HR over the last 20 minutes is a good estimate. Benchmark 1 corrects it.
q2: Does it work for doubles with different levels?
a2: Yes. The slower runner sets the pace, stations are split on both partners' strengths and you both see the same team prediction.
a3: Only you see your data. In a doubles team your partner sees your sessions and benchmarks; nobody else does.

bm.title: A benchmark that tells the truth
bm.sub: Most apps take your fastest number and run with it. Benchmrk looks at your heart rate too.
bm.case: Mark runs his threshold test at 3:48/km — but with an average HR of 181, above his threshold HR of 178.
